items.title: Linux sandbox: /proc fallback does not detect the bubblewrap 0.12 error ("Can't mount proc on /proc")

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: sandbox
labels.description: Issues related to permissions or sandboxing

labels.name: CLI
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex CLI

items.body:
### What version of Codex CLI is running?

codex-cli 0.160.1. The same check is on `main`.

### Platform

Alpine Linux 3.23 (musl), aarch64, in an Apple container VM. System bubblewrap 0.12.0 (Alpine package `bubblewrap`). The process runs as root with full capabilities.

### What happened?

`codex sandbox -- true` fails with `bwrap: Can't mount proc on /proc: Operation not permitted`. Every sandboxed command fails the same way.

The container runtime masks parts of `/proc` (tmpfs over `kcore`, `keys` and `timer_list`, read-only binds over `/proc/sys/*`). So the kernel refuses a fresh `/proc` mount in a new user namespace. Codex has a fallback for this case: `preflight_proc_mount_support` runs `bwrap --proc /proc` and, on a mount failure, retries without a fresh `/proc`.

The fallback does not start. `is_proc_mount_failure` in `codex-rs/linux-sandbox/src/linux_run_main.rs` requires the text `/newroot/proc`. bubblewrap 0.12.0 prints the path inside the sandbox (`op->dest`, here `/proc`). Versions 0.8.0 to 0.11.0 print `arg1` (`/newroot/proc`).

### Evidence

- A logging `bwrap` wrapper on PATH shows the preflight call with `--proc /proc` and then the real call, again with `--proc /proc`.
- The preflight stderr is `bwrap: Can't mount proc on /proc: Operation not permitted`.
- With the system `bwrap` hidden, Codex uses its bundled `codex-resources/bwrap`. That binary prints `Can't mount proc on /newroot/proc`, the fallback starts, and `codex sandbox -P :workspace` works: the workspace is writable, `/etc` is read-only, and the network is blocked.
- With the `/proc` masks removed in a private mount namespace, the system `bwrap` 0.12.0 also works.

### Expected behavior

The fallback detects the bubblewrap 0.12 message too. One possible fix: accept `Can't mount proc on` with either `/newroot/proc` or `/proc`.

### Impact

Codex shows a startup warning when no system bubblewrap is on PATH. Users who install bubblewrap from a distribution with 0.12 to remove that warning lose the sandbox in containers that mask `/proc`. Today the workaround is to remove the system bubblewrap.

Thank you for the bundled `bwrap` and the `/proc` fallback. Both work well in this environment.

# Windows 10: Computer Use não captura Minecraft nem Bloco de Notas

## Ambiente
- Data da ocorrência: 8 de outubro de 2026.
- Windows x64; versão retornada pelo sistema: Microsoft Windows NT 10.0.19045.0.
- Plugin Computer Use: 26.1002.52244.
- Versão exata do aplicativo e plano da conta: não coletados.

## Problema
O Computer Use encontra as janelas dos aplicativos, mas não retorna capturas de tela. O problema foi reproduzido repetidamente no Minecraft for Windows (Bedrock) e também no Bloco de Notas clássico.

Erros exatos:
```text
FrameArrived timed out: timed out waiting on channel
window capture timed out: timed out waiting on channel
```

## Reprodução observada
1. Inicializar @oai/sky na sessão Node do Computer Use.
2. Usar list_apps para selecionar a única janela retornada do Minecraft.
3. Resolver a janela com get_window e ativá-la com activate_window.
4. Chamar get_window_state({ window }), com captura habilitada por padrão.
5. A captura termina com um dos erros acima.
6. Atualizar a seleção com list_windows e get_window e repetir: a captura continua falhando.
7. Repetir com o Bloco de Notas: o plugin abriu o aplicativo e encontrou sua janela sem título, mas a captura inicial e a nova tentativa também falharam.

## Resultado esperado
Receber uma imagem da janela selecionada para permitir a inspeção visual e a continuidade da tarefa autorizada.

## Impacto
A tarefa de quebrar a madeira de uma árvore no Minecraft não pôde ser executada. Nenhum bloco do jogo foi alterado.

## Observações
- Uma tentativa inicial foi interrompida com Escape. As tentativas posteriores autorizadas retornaram os erros de captura, não o aviso de interrupção.
- Reinicialização do aplicativo ou do Windows, mudança para modo janela, captura somente de acessibilidade e diagnóstico da GPU não foram verificados nesta sessão.
- Há relatos semelhantes: https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/50749, https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/51358 e https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/35446. A mesma causa não foi confirmada.
- Este relato não inclui conversas pessoais, nome de usuário local, capturas de tela ou logs completos.

Solicito investigação da falha e orientação sobre os diagnósticos necessários para confirmar a causa.

items.body:
## Documentation issue type

Documentation is missing

## Where did you find it?

https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/config-file/config-reference.md, the `model_providers.<id>.*` entries (lines 1028-1157 of the Markdown page).

## Summary

codex-cli 0.162.0 added a `[model_providers.<id>.capabilities]` table for custom Responses-compatible providers (#50459). The table has two keys: `external_web_access` (boolean) and `remote_compaction` (`"v2"` or `"unsupported"`). The configuration reference lists 21 `model_providers.<id>.*` keys, including `supports_standalone_web_search`, but has no entry for this table or its keys. None of the 180 pages linked from the docs index at https://learn.chatgpt.com/llms.txt mentions `external_web_access` or `remote_compaction`.

## Problem to solve

Users of a custom provider who want to stop hosted web search from reaching the live web, or who want local compaction instead of a provider compaction protocol, cannot find these settings in the reference. The PR description and `codex-rs/core/config.schema.json` are the only descriptions. The exact names matter. With `--strict-config`, a mistyped key inside the table is rejected. Without strict mode, the same typo is silently ignored and the provider keeps its default.

## Proposed behavior

The configuration reference documents `model_providers.<id>.capabilities` and its two keys, with types, allowed values and defaults that match the shipped schema:

- `capabilities.external_web_access`: boolean; whether hosted web search may access the live web.
- `capabilities.remote_compaction`: `v2` sends `compaction_trigger` items through the Responses endpoint; `unsupported` uses local compaction.
- If either key is omitted, the provider keeps its existing default for that capability.

A short example could also go in Advanced Config next to the existing `supports_standalone_web_search` example. The sample config file could also gain one.

## Acceptance criteria

- The configuration reference has entries for `model_providers.<id>.capabilities`, `model_providers.<id>.capabilities.external_web_access` and `model_providers.<id>.capabilities.remote_compaction`. Their types and allowed values match the `ModelProviderCapabilities` and `RemoteCompactionSupport` definitions in `codex-rs/core/config.schema.json`.
- Any documented example TOML for the table loads under `codex --strict-config` on 0.162.0 or later.

## Affected area

Configuration reference page (custom model provider keys); optionally Advanced Config and the sample configuration page.

## Non-goals

Changing the behavior or names of the capability keys.

## Supporting context

- Schema at tag `rust-v0.162.0`: `codex-rs/core/config.schema.json` (`ModelProviderCapabilities` near line 2731 with `additionalProperties: false`, and `RemoteCompactionSupport`). Source: `codex-rs/model-provider-info/src/capabilities.rs`.
- Observed with codex-cli 0.162.0 on macOS arm64, using an isolated `CODEX_HOME` and no credentials. With `--strict-config`, the config below loaded and the run continued to the trusted-directory check. Replacing the two keys with `not_a_key = true` failed with exit status 1 and ``unknown configuration field `model_providers.custom.capabilities.not_a_key` ``. Without `--strict-config`, that typo config loaded with no warning and also reached the trusted-directory check.

```toml
[model_providers.custom]
name = "Custom"
base_url = "https://example.invalid/v1"

[model_providers.custom.capabilities]
external_web_access = false
remote_compaction = "unsupported"
```

- Related open issues about remote compaction for custom providers: #42313 and #37010. Whether this table resolves either was not checked.
- The GitHub release notes for 0.162.0 announce the feature in one line ("Configure live web access and remote compaction capabilities for custom Responses-compatible model providers.") but do not name the keys. Whether any page outside the llms.txt index documents them is unknown.

## Triage assessment

- Impact level: not-applicable
- Assessment status: not-applicable
- Impact basis: This is missing reference documentation for a new configuration surface. No existing documented behavior fails.
- Workaround status: not-applicable
- Workaround basis: No defect is involved. The keys work when they are configured from the PR description or the JSON schema.

items.title: fix(docs): `/copy` docs say it copies the latest output immediately, but it opens a block selection first

labels.name: documentation
labels.description: Improvements or additions to documentation

labels.name: TUI
labels.description: Issues related to the terminal user interface: text input, menus and dialogs, and terminal display

labels.name: CLI
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex CLI

items.body:
## Documentation issue type

Documentation is incorrect, Documentation is missing

## Where did you find it?

https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/developer-commands.md?surface=cli, section "Copy the latest response with `/copy`" (lines 617-628 of the Markdown page), the `/copy` row of the slash-command table (line 378), and the keyboard tip at line 326. The same text appears in the aggregate https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/codex-manual.md (lines 17547, 20492 and 20728).

## Summary

The CLI slash-command reference says that typing `/copy` and pressing Enter copies the latest completed Codex output to the clipboard. In the shipped TUI, `/copy` copies nothing at first. It opens a selection, and the user then chooses the whole response or one block of it. The default full-screen transcript in 0.162.0 enters an in-transcript copy mode, and inline mode and earlier releases open a "Copy to clipboard" picker. The page mentions neither, so its stated result is wrong in both modes. Ctrl+O still copies the whole response directly, as the page says.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Read the `/copy` section of the page above.
2. Inspect the `SlashCommand::Copy` arm in `codex-rs/tui/src/chatwidget/slash_dispatch.rs`, which calls `show_copy_picker()`, and `codex-rs/tui/src/chatwidget/copy_picker.rs` at the release tag under Runtime or environment. This assumes no `/status` output is pending, because after `/status` both paths offer status fields instead.
   - If the TUI owns the transcript, `show_copy_picker` sends `AppEvent::SelectTranscriptCopy`. The app then calls `transcript_view.begin_copy_mode`. With the defaults (`tui.fullscreen_transcript = true` and `tui.alternate_screen = "auto"`), the TUI owns the transcript, except in Terminal.app over SSH.
   - Otherwise it opens a selection view titled "Copy to clipboard", which lists "Whole response" and each code block and blockquote.
   - In both cases nothing is copied until the user confirms a choice.
3. Not executed for this report: in an interactive 0.162.0 session with default settings, wait for a completed response that contains a fenced `sh` code block, then type `/copy` and press Enter. Per the source and the upstream tests named under Evidence, the transcript enters copy mode with the latest response selected as "Whole response". Up and Down (or `j` and `k`) move between blocks, and Enter or the copy key copies the selection. With `--no-alt-screen`, `tui.alternate_screen = "never"` or `tui.fullscreen_transcript = false`, or on 0.160.1 or 0.161.0, the same steps open the "Copy to clipboard" picker. There, pressing `1` copies the whole response and `2` copies the code block.

## Expected behavior

The page should describe what the shipped `/copy` does. It opens a selection of the latest response, either as transcript copy mode in the default full-screen transcript or as a picker in inline mode. The user then copies the whole response or one of its blocks. The page should also say that Ctrl+O copies the whole response without a selection step.

## Actual behavior

The page says: "Type `/copy` and press Enter. Expected: Codex copies the latest completed Codex output to your clipboard." The table row says "Copy the latest completed Codex output", and line 326 says "Press Ctrl+O or run `/copy` to copy the latest completed Codex output". The page does not mention a selection step or partial copies. In every build checked, `/copy` opens a selection instead of copying. From 0.162.0 on, the default full-screen transcript uses in-transcript copy mode. The picker remains for inline mode and is the only path in 0.160.1 and 0.161.0. The slash popup describes the command as "copy the last response or part of it". The 0.162.0 release notes announce "Navigate and copy transcript blocks with `/copy`".

## Evidence

- Expected source: shipped TUI behavior at `rust-v0.162.0`. The relevant files are `codex-rs/tui/src/slash_command.rs` line 108 (popup description), `codex-rs/tui/src/chatwidget/copy_picker.rs` (the owned-transcript handoff and the picker), `codex-rs/tui/src/transcript_mode.rs`, and `codex-rs/tui/src/transcript_view/copy_mode.rs`. The default for `tui.fullscreen_transcript` is in `codex-rs/config/src/types.rs`. Upstream tests cover both paths. `owned_copy_opens_transcript_selection` in `codex-rs/tui/src/chatwidget/tests/copy_export_picker_tests.rs` covers the owned mode. `slash_copy_picker_uses_completed_commentary_during_active_turn` and `slash_copy_state_tracks_plan_item_completion` in `codex-rs/tui/src/chatwidget/tests/slash_commands.rs` cover the inline picker; they force terminal transcript mode and assert that the popup lists "Whole response" and "sh code".
- Failure source: the `/copy` section, table row and keyboard tip of the developer commands page, quoted under Actual behavior.
- Evidence provenance: static
- Local verification: static-proof
- Reproduction completeness: complete

Runtime reproduction was not run, because a completed response requires a signed-in model turn and this check used no credentials or model turns. The static proof covers several points: the supported entry point (typing `/copy` in the composer), the dispatch to `show_copy_picker`, the condition that selects transcript copy mode or the picker, the defaults that make transcript copy mode the usual 0.162.0 path, and the upstream tests for each path. The Ctrl+O path (`prepare_last_response_copy` in `codex-rs/tui/src/chatwidget/interaction.rs`) copies the whole response directly, consistent with the page's Ctrl+O sentence.

## Restoration check

Today the page says that `/copy` followed by Enter copies the latest output and mentions no selection step. The fix restores agreement when the `/copy` section, the table row and the keyboard tip describe the selection step for the default full-screen transcript. Its whole-response and block choices must be included, and so must the inline-mode picker. A page that describes only the inline picker would still misstate the default 0.162.0 behavior. Ctrl+O should remain documented as the direct whole-response copy.

## Runtime or environment

- Documentation pages fetched on 2026-10-08 (Pacific time).
- Source checked at tags `rust-v0.160.1`, `rust-v0.161.0` and `rust-v0.162.0` (the latest stable release when checked), and at `main` commit c9e0fffbbc05c36478686444f6ab1edbadfe2768. The owned-transcript copy mode handoff is present in 0.162.0 and `main` but not in 0.160.1 or 0.161.0.

## Triage assessment

- Impact level: P3
- Assessment status: supported
- Impact basis: The defect is wording in reference documentation. A reader who follows the page gets a selection step instead of an immediate copy and needs one more keypress. No data is lost and no workflow is blocked.
- Workaround status: available
- Workaround basis: Ctrl+O copies the whole latest response directly in both transcript modes. Without pending `/status` output, both selections start on the latest whole response, so pressing Enter (or `1` in the picker) copies it.

## Documentation issue type

Documentation is incorrect, Documentation is missing

## Where did you find it?

https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/developer-commands.md?surface=cli, section "List MCP tools with `/mcp`" (line 866 of the Markdown page) and the `/mcp` row of the slash-command table (line 389). The same text appears in the aggregate https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/codex-manual.md.

## Summary

The CLI slash-command reference says `/mcp` accepts only `verbose` and that any other argument shows the command usage. Since codex-cli 0.161.0 (#49290) the TUI also accepts `/mcp login <name>`, which starts MCP OAuth sign-in for the named server from the active session. The page does not mention this form and tells readers that it prints usage.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Read the `/mcp` section of the page above.
2. Inspect the `SlashCommand::Mcp` arm in `codex-rs/tui/src/chatwidget/slash_dispatch.rs` (around lines 844-863 at the release tag under Runtime or environment). It handles `verbose`, handles `login <name>` by sending `AppEvent::StartMcpLogin` for the active thread, and prints `Usage: /mcp [verbose | login <name>]` for anything else.
3. Not executed for this report: in an interactive session with an OAuth MCP server configured, type `/mcp login <server>`. Per the source and the upstream tests named under Evidence, the TUI starts sign-in instead of printing usage. The slash popup also describes `/mcp` as "list MCP tools; use /mcp verbose or /mcp login <name>".

## Expected behavior

The page should describe the `/mcp` arguments that the shipped TUI accepts, `verbose` and `login <name>`, and should say that only other arguments print the usage message.

## Actual behavior

The page says: "Use `/mcp verbose` to include detailed server diagnostics. If you pass anything other than `verbose`, Codex shows the command usage." The table row says only to "add `verbose` for server details". Neither mentions `/mcp login <name>`. In every build checked from 0.161.0 on, `/mcp login <name>` emits a sign-in request, and the usage string itself lists `login <name>`. In 0.160.1 the same arm accepted only `verbose` and printed `Usage: /mcp [verbose]`, so the page matches that older release.

## Evidence

- Expected source: shipped TUI behavior at `rust-v0.162.0`: `codex-rs/tui/src/slash_command.rs` line 152 (popup description) and the `SlashCommand::Mcp` arm in `codex-rs/tui/src/chatwidget/slash_dispatch.rs`, covered by upstream tests `slash_mcp_login_targets_the_active_thread` and `slash_mcp_invalid_args_show_usage` in `codex-rs/tui/src/chatwidget/tests/slash_commands.rs`.
- Failure source: the `/mcp` section and table row of the developer commands page, quoted under Actual behavior.
- Evidence provenance: static
- Local verification: static-proof
- Reproduction completeness: complete

Runtime reproduction was not run, because an interactive session requires sign-in and this check used no credentials. The static proof covers the supported entry point (typing `/mcp login <name>` in the composer), the dispatch arm that parses it, and the upstream unit tests that assert it sends `StartMcpLogin` and that other arguments print the new usage string.

## Restoration check

Today the page says that any argument other than `verbose` prints usage, and it omits `/mcp login <name>`. The fix restores agreement when the page documents `/mcp login <name>`, including what it starts and that it needs an active session, and applies the usage-message statement only to other arguments, consistent with `Usage: /mcp [verbose | login <name>]`.

## Runtime or environment

- Documentation page fetched on 2026-10-08 (Pacific time).
- Source checked at tags `rust-v0.160.1`, `rust-v0.161.0` and `rust-v0.162.0` (the latest stable release when checked), and at `main` commit c9e0fffbbc05c36478686444f6ab1edbadfe2768. All three builds from 0.161.0 on have the same `/mcp` handling.

## Triage assessment

- Impact level: P3
- Assessment status: supported
- Impact basis: The defect is a wording error and omission in reference documentation. Following the page breaks nothing, but it tells readers that the in-session sign-in form prints usage.
- Workaround status: available
- Workaround basis: The CLI command `codex mcp login <server-name>`, documented on the MCP page, signs in from a terminal, and the TUI slash popup shows the `login <name>` form.

Earlier sandbox logs showed a separate setup-refresh failure caused by Windows error 32 when opening node_repl.exe or VCRUNTIME140_1.dll in the shared Codex runtime. I cannot establish whether that earlier failure and the current split-root rejection have the same cause.
Expected: a supported sandbox configuration should allow the read-only command to run while preserving its access boundaries, or provide an actionable setup error. I am not requesting a sandbox bypass.
Feedback reference: 01a11adb-f112-7080-a47a-07f6c3e30065
Related report with the same split-root error: https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/32168
Related report about the earlier runtime file-lock error: https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/51906

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

Feedback ID: 01a11adb-f112-7080-a47a-07f6c3e30065

### What is the expected behavior?

The delegated task should run the authorized read-only command within an enforceable sandbox. If its permission configuration is incompatible with the Windows sandbox implementation, the app should provide a clear, supported recovery path without requiring unrestricted execution.

### Additional information

Earlier logs showed a separate runtime ACL setup failure with Windows error 32 on node_repl.exe or VCRUNTIME140_1.dll. Later log entries show successful commands in other contexts. The relationship between these failures is unknown. No process has been identified as the cause, and there is no evidence of conflicting project-file writes.

items.body:
## Problem

On Fedora Linux, a full-access thread changed to a managed `:workspace` permission profile during a goal-continuation boundary. Tool commands then lost GitHub connectivity and write access to Git metadata and sibling worktrees. A CLI client attached to that thread was launched with `--dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox`, but the effective restricted context persisted. Restarting the shared daemon did not restore access in the attached conversation.

A subsequent launch using `--no-daemon` and the same bypass flag passed all diagnostic checks. **The recovered conversation is a fork with a different thread ID**, according to `session_meta.forked_from_id`; this is not proof that the original thread recovered, nor a controlled demonstration that the daemon alone caused the problem.

This is an observed permission-state/lifecycle problem, not a claim that the sandbox incorrectly enforced its received restricted policy. The source of the policy change remains unknown.

## Environment

- CLI and shared app-server daemon during diagnostics: `0.162.0`; this was the latest stable release when checked on 2026-10-08.
- Platform: Fedora 44, `Linux 7.2.7-200.fc44.x86_64 x86_64`.
- Installation: npm CLI plus the managed daemon package; matching versions.
- Terminal: SSH terminal, `TERM=xterm-256color`; emulator and multiplexer versions not established.
- Model in current settings/doctor: `gpt-6.1-sol`; not established as model-specific.
- Subscription: not established in these diagnostics.
- Integration context: the original current thread records `source=vscode` and `originator=claude-command-center`. It was subsequently accessed through a CLI `resume` client. This is a multi-client/orchestration-integrated history, not a proven clean CLI-only reproduction. Two older affected histories record `originator=codex-tui`.
- User config had no explicit top-level `sandbox_mode` or `approval_policy`, and no explicit `features.daemon_auto_start`; the effective daemon auto-start feature was enabled.

## Evidence

### Current incident: actual local rollout and log records

Thread IDs and paths below are anonymous aliases. All times are UTC.

| Record | Time | Observation |
|---|---|---|
| Session A, first `turn_context` | 2026-10-08 15:49:43.930 | `sandbox_policy={"type":"danger-full-access"}`, `approval_policy=never` |
| Session A, `thread_settings_applied` | 2026-10-08 19:38:39.618 | Managed restricted filesystem/network profile, `active_permission_profile.id=":workspace"`; repository root writable but its `.git`, `.agents`, `.codex`, and `.aws` explicitly read-only; sibling worktree outside writable roots |
| Session A, next `turn_context` | 2026-10-08 19:38:40.900 | `sandbox_policy={"type":"workspace-write","network_access":false,"exclude_tmpdir_env_var":false,"exclude_slash_tmp":false}`, `approval_policy=never` |
| Session A, next user input | 2026-10-08 19:38:40.903 | Internal goal-continuation input |
| Session A-fork, first `turn_context` | 2026-10-08 19:57:53.597 | `danger-full-access`, `approval_policy=never`; `session_meta.source=cli`, `forked_from_id=A` |

The original rollout was created under CLI `0.161.0`; the CLI and daemon were independently confirmed as `0.162.0` during the failure investigation. A rollout's creation version is not necessarily the version of every later turn.

The log database at the downgrade boundary contains a core submission with:

```text
operation="turn_input"
op=TurnInput {
  requested_settings: ThreadSettingsOverrides {
    approval_policy: None,
    approvals_reviewer: None,
    sandbox_policy: None,
    permission_profile: None
  }
}
```

This is a useful tracing lead, not proof that no earlier client/settings path supplied the managed profile. There is no identified intentional permission-change request from the user in the nearby conversation.

### Inside/outside controls and recovery

An ordinary terminal on the same machine could resolve `github.com` and `api.github.com`, received HTTP 200 from `https://api.github.com`, and successfully created automatically cleaned temporary files in both `<REPO-A>/.git` and `<REPO-A-WORKTREES>/scan-change`.

Inside the affected conversation, the corresponding checks returned:

```text
getent hosts github.com api.github.com
# exit 2, no output

gh issue view <ISSUE> --repo <OWNER>/<REPO> --json number,state
# exit 1:
error connecting to api.github.com
check your internet connection or https://githubstatus.com

git ls-remote https://github.com/<OWNER>/<REPO>.git refs/heads/main
# exit 128:
fatal: unable to access 'https://github.com/<OWNER>/<REPO>.git/': Could not resolve host: github.com

# Python tempfile.TemporaryFile in each affected directory:
<REPO-A>/.git OSError(30, 'Read-only file system')
<REPO-A-WORKTREES>/scan-change OSError(30, 'Read-only file system')
```

Process inspection outside the session confirmed a client command of this form:

```sh
codex --dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox resume <THREAD-A>
```

Both `codex --version` and `codex app-server daemon version` reported `0.162.0`. The latter reported a running PID-backed shared daemon. `codex app-server daemon restart` returned `status=restarted`; the next diagnostic turn in the affected conversation still produced the same DNS, GitHub CLI, and read-only errors.

After exiting/restarting with:

```sh
codex --no-daemon --dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox   -C <REPO-A> resume <THREAD-A>
```

the new fork passed all three diagnostics: DNS exit 0, GitHub CLI exit 0 with valid issue JSON, and both temporary-file write checks reported `WRITE OK`. This workaround changes both daemon participation and thread identity, so those variables are not yet isolated.

### Other local histories reviewed

A bounded read-only review of the 35 most recently updated root CLI/VS Code session histories found two additional earlier sessions with actual full-access → restricted → full-access transitions and matching tool failures. These are distinct local occurrences, not copies of this conversation:

| Anonymous session | Initial full access | Downgrade | Actual failure after downgrade | Full access restored |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| B, different repository | 2026-09-28 02:46:51.826 | 13:11:41.685: `workspace-write`, `network_access=false`, approvals still `never` | `error connecting to api.github.com` at 13:11:55.806 and later attempts | 14:55:38.358; user input explicitly mentions launching with the bypass flag |
| C, another repository | 2026-09-28 03:16:48.320 | 13:09:57.528: same restricted policy, approvals still `never` | SSH exit 255, `socket: Operation not permitted` at 13:10:54.707 | 16:02:41.881; user also reports a host upgrade/reboot, so the recovery cause is confounded |

Both older sessions have creation metadata CLI `0.157.1`; their exact executable version at each later transition is unverified. These histories show recurrence of the symptom, not proof of a single root cause across versions. No full private transcripts are attached.

### Source references checked at the 0.162.0 release commit

These establish the relevant expected behavior and tracing surfaces, not the faulty line:

- [`codex-rs/cli/src/main.rs:2013-2026`](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/c1382380de69521303b416720a52f42d51af6248/codex-rs/cli/src/main.rs#L2013-L2026): bypass maps to `AskForApproval::Never` and `SandboxMode::DangerFullAccess` in the inspected config-building path.
- [`codex-rs/tui/src/cli.rs:83-85`](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/c1382380de69521303b416720a52f42d51af6248/codex-rs/tui/src/cli.rs#L83-L85): `--no-daemon` is explicitly defined to run without the shared server even when one is running.
- [`codex-rs/core/src/session/handlers.rs:480-487`](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/c1382380de69521303b416720a52f42d51af6248/codex-rs/core/src/session/handlers.rs#L480-L487): the core submission logging surface for the observed `TurnInput` entry.
- [`codex-rs/app-server/src/request_processors/thread_lifecycle.rs:760-795`](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/c1382380de69521303b416720a52f42d51af6248/codex-rs/app-server/src/request_processors/thread_lifecycle.rs#L760-L795): resume response includes the config snapshot's sandbox, approval policy, and active permission profile.

## Steps / observed reproduction sequence

This is the observed sequence, not a deterministic minimal reproduction:

1. Run a long-lived full-access thread with goal continuation and orchestration/other-client participation.
2. Access/resume the thread through a CLI launched with the bypass flag while the shared daemon is available.
3. At a later continuation, observe `thread_settings_applied` selecting `:workspace`, followed by `workspace-write` with networking disabled despite the prior full-access context.
4. Run the DNS, GitHub CLI, and temporary-file probes below inside and outside the session; observe the differential above.
5. Restart the shared daemon; in this incident that did not restore the affected conversation's effective permissions.
6. Exit/restart through `--no-daemon` with the same bypass flag. In this incident this produced a new fork with working diagnostics.

The timing of step 2 relative to the first downgrade is not established. The precise triggering client/RPC and the reason recovery forked instead of reusing the original thread remain open questions.

Filesystem probe, which cleans up its own temporary files:

```python
import tempfile
for directory in ("<REPO-A>/.git", "<REPO-A-WORKTREES>/scan-change"):
    try:
        with tempfile.TemporaryFile(dir=directory):
            print(directory, "WRITE OK")
    except OSError as error:
        print(directory, repr(error))
```

## Expected

An existing full-access thread should preserve its explicitly selected effective permission context across goal continuation and client resume unless an intentional policy change overrides it. If attaching to an already-running thread retains a different policy than the CLI launch requested, disclose that clearly and provide a supported way to reconcile it. Respect required managed security policy; do not weaken sandbox enforcement as a workaround.

## Proposed approach

Trace the settings resolution at goal-continuation, active-thread attachment/resume, and fork boundaries, including multi-client/orchestration inputs. Record which source selects `:workspace`, and compare that with explicit CLI overrides and the existing effective thread settings. Test both an already-running shared-daemon thread and a stopped thread, plus a clean CLI-only control. Add regression coverage for preservation/explicit change of permission context and for accurate reporting of active-thread settings.

Doctor should make clear when it has not inspected active thread overrides; its general `ok` currently cannot establish that this thread's requested permissions were honored.

## Related reports / deduplication

Searched open and closed issues. These are related leads, not asserted identical root causes:

- #14068 (open): older direct app-server bypass/child-sandbox mismatch; no equivalent shared-daemon active-thread/continuation/fork controls established there.
- #22090, #24300, #29610 (closed as completed): earlier goal/heartbeat permission-context downgrade reports. This report supplies a later Linux occurrence with matching CLI/daemon versions, actual settings events, cross-session histories, and outside/inside controls.
- #29503 and #15310 (open): macOS app/new-thread and scheduled-automation default-policy problems; this incident is an existing Linux thread with a bypass CLI attached.
- #35514 (open): iOS remote access deletes host configuration; no such config mutation is established here.

## Provenance and privacy

Filed at the affected user's explicit request after reviewing their local histories. Paths, usernames, thread IDs, PIDs, repository names and issue numbers from private work are anonymized. Software versions, timestamps, policy fields, exit codes and error messages are retained. No raw session transcripts or credentials are attached. The orchestration integration is disclosed because its role has not been ruled out.

items.body:
### What version of the Codex App are you using (From “About Codex” dialog)?

ChatGPT desktop for Linux **26.903.61454** (`chatgpt-desktop-bin 26.903.61454-1`). Version obtained from the installed package and `resources/linux-package-metadata.json`.

This is a local Arch repackaging of OpenAI's official Debian package. The installed `/usr/lib/chatgpt/ChatGPT` binary was verified byte-for-byte by SHA-256 against the binary inside that Debian package. No binary patch was applied. This has not been retested on the latest app release.

### What subscription do you have?

Not specified in this report.

### What platform is your computer?

- Omarchy 4.0.3 (Arch Linux), x86_64
- `uname -mprs`: `Linux 7.2.3-arch1-3 x86_64 unknown`
- Hyprland `0.56.2-2`; XWayland `24.1.13-1`
- The crash is in the application's X11 drag-and-drop handling.

### What issue are you seeing?

Dragging an image from Gmail into the ChatGPT desktop app terminated its main process with **SIGTRAP**. Two systemd core dumps captured the same failing binary offset, the same file-URL payload, and the same 67-versus-66-byte mismatch.

Two crashes were captured during the same session, including one after the app was relaunched. Exact timestamps, timezone, and process IDs are omitted for privacy.

The JPEG involved remains present and decoded successfully with `djpeg`. There was no OOM-kill evidence. Other threads in the first core were waiting in event loops, polling, or condition variables.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

1. Open the ChatGPT Linux desktop app in the Hyprland session.
2. Open Gmail in a browser and drag the image into ChatGPT. This action was confirmed by the user.
3. Observe the application terminate with SIGTRAP while handling the drag.

The core payload is a local `file://` URL for the JPEG, **67 ASCII bytes long with no NUL bytes**. The local JPEG had finished downloading about 1.3 seconds before the first trap. Browser identity and the component that supplied the incorrect transfer format have not been established. Reproduction with arbitrary other images has not been tested.

### What is the expected behavior?

The image should attach, or an invalid drag-data format should be rejected safely. Malformed external drag data should not terminate the desktop application's main process.

### Additional information

#### Core and disassembly findings

The URL was being processed in the `text/x-moz-url` branch. That format is handled as UTF-16, but the captured payload was ordinary single-byte ASCII.

At the failure, in both cores:

```text
R15 = 0x43 (67 incoming bytes)
RCX = 0x42 (66 destination bytes)
crash PC = ChatGPT + 0xd72e214
```

The disassembly resizes a two-byte-character string to `67 / 2 = 33` characters (66 bytes), compares its byte size with the original 67-byte input, and branches to `int3` on inequality. The saved PC points to the following `ud2` instruction. This is an explicit failed size check.

Common leading main-thread frames, reported by systemd-coredump as offsets in ChatGPT:

```text
#0  +0xd72e214
#1  +0xd72e7f9
#2  +0xd73ee43
#3  +0xd555963
#4  +0xa2235f8
#5  +0xa2252de
#6  +0xe5c0b22
```

ELF build ID: `502f6ee538f93624bbbd768cb22941f875a526b4`

Binary SHA-256: `fda09eaccd809821e71b33275bd20cac20b8bd587f1756471fb705cd59e4542d`

Debug symbols for the application were unavailable, including from Arch debuginfod. The source mapping below is inferred from the disassembly and matching Chromium code, not a symbolized application backtrace:

- [`XOSExchangeDataProvider::GetURLs`](https://github.com/chromium/chromium/blob/main/ui/base/x/x11_os_exchange_data_provider.cc): handles Mozilla URL data as UTF-16 via `SelectionData::AssignTo(std::u16string*)`.
- [`RefCountedMemoryToString16`](https://github.com/chromium/chromium/blob/main/ui/base/x/selection_utils.cc): resizes the output to `memory->size() / 2u`, then copies the entire byte span into it.

The immediate failure is in the app's handling of malformed drag data. The evidence does not establish whether the source browser or the desktop transfer path supplied the incorrectly formatted data. It does not implicate Omarchy-specific configuration or packaging.

Suggested area to investigate: validate odd-length/non-UTF-16 Mozilla URL data before conversion, and trace why this transfer is delivered as `text/x-moz-url`. Selecting the already-downloaded JPEG with the attachment picker is a suggested workaround; it has not been tested as part of this investigation.

A local executor's thread-read API could read that second conversation, while dot's direct route could not. This suggests a difference between the access paths; it does not establish the root cause. Creating an extra conversation just to relay messages is not a practical replacement for direct access to the original task.

### Reproduction

1. Keep the Mac connected and authorized for dot tasks.
2. Manually create a Codex conversation inside a local project and use it normally.
3. Copy its conversation link to dot.
4. Ask dot to read its progress or continue that specific task.
5. The direct read fails with the placement-format error above; a send may report that the thread was not found.

After I identify and authorize access to an existing local task, dot should be able to read it, or explain a specific missing permission. I am not asking for automatic access to every conversation.

In a separate dot-created inspection task, the Mac repeatedly showed a Computer Use prompt asking whether ChatGPT could use **T3 Code Nightly**. I selected **Always allow** several times, but the task continued waiting for approval.

The separate execution workspace can retrieve the official Mozilla archive over HTTPS. Its networking must not be treated as proof that native desktop applications have the same access.

## Scope and related reports

- This report concerns current cloud-desktop networking and the supported configuration for a separately launched browser.
- [#52217](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/52217) covers the preceding workspace/content-loss observations and recovery. The relationship between that event and this connection failure is unknown.
- [#51608](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/51608) covers inconsistent approval handling during earlier CA restoration. The current CA import was completed and verified with explicit confirmation; that is not the remaining blocker.

No infrastructure root cause, site-wide outage, or universal Firefox incompatibility is established.

- Official Mozilla Firefox **157.0.1**, Linux x86-64, build **20261005135250**.
- Mozilla archive: **88,413,848 bytes**, SHA-256 `0d92bf39cdd174f5f361008509310bdefbce72a57ca10523a43b32d62dc699b6`, matched against the current official Mozilla SHA256SUMS.

- Exact cloud backend deployment and desktop image version are unavailable.

During approximately **18:36–18:39**, HTTPS requests from the actual desktop terminal to both the Mozilla download redirector and its official installer CDN failed:

```text
curl: (7) Failed to connect to download.mozilla.org port 443

```

Firefox was then visibly launched on the cloud desktop. Its attempt to open ChatGPT ended with:

```text
Unable to connect
Firefox can't connect to the server at chatgpt.com.
```

### Exact existing platform CA restored and verified

At **18:59:45**, the specifically confirmed existing public `nebula-dns.crt` was imported into Firefox as a website/TLS-server authority.

- NSS readback showed `C,,`: trusted to issue TLS server certificates, with no added email or code-signing trust.
- The imported fingerprint matched before import, after import, and after normal browser shutdown.
- TLS validation and hostname checks were retained. No browser-generated certificate warning was bypassed.

A subsequent normal launch still ended on “Unable to connect”; no certificate warning or login page appeared.

### Failure observed before TLS

At **19:03:02**, a bounded read-only diagnostic attempted a TCP connection to `chatgpt.com:443`, with normal certificate and hostname validation prepared for any subsequent TLS handshake:

```text
stage: TCP connection
errorClass: OSError
error: [Errno 101] Network is unreachable
```

- **Use system proxy settings** selected.
- Empty manual HTTP, HTTPS and SOCKS host fields; displayed ports 0.

At **19:14:51**, one additional deliberate restart was performed:

2. Confirm its window was absent.
3. Independently confirm neither `firefox` nor `firefox-bin` was running.
4. Launch Firefox once with https://chatgpt.com/.

At **19:17:10**, the resulting page was again **“Unable to connect.”** No retry loop was used. Account/login status remains unverified because the site UI was never reached.

If native desktop applications require a platform proxy or another supplied configuration, provision it through a supported route or provide exact supported setup guidance. The current visible/system settings expose no usable endpoint to restore. It should not be necessary to infer private endpoints from another browser or change security settings speculatively.

A host can reject a request for an unknown session while its lease streams remain open. Keeping that session binding prevents subsequent execution from recovering.

## What changed

## Testing

Add regression coverage for recovery with lease streams still open, no replay of failed execution, and preservation of session state after `INVALID_ARGUMENT`. Add a cancellation-race test confirming that a late tool-completion `NOT_FOUND` leaves the session open.

None in the initialization-only probe. No `thread/start`, `account/read`, or `turn/start` request was sent.

### What terminal emulator and version are you using (if applicable)?

Programmatic stdio subprocess. PowerShell was used for local diagnostics; an interactive terminal-emulator version was not collected.

Not collected. This report preserves a bounded initialization-only diagnostic scope; no new native CLI launch or raw diagnostic archive was collected for publication.

### What issue are you seeing?

The native `app-server` exits before answering a valid `initialize` request. The latest retained initialization-only probe reached stdout EOF at 30.313 seconds and exited with code 1, before its 45-second watchdog. It sent only `initialize`; there was no valid initialization response and no `initialized` notification. Account, thread, and model setup were not reached by the client.

The complete stderr capture was 611 bytes and was not truncated. Its sanitized projection retained these ordered fragments; original line boundaries were flattened by the earlier local observer:

```text
(os error 5) ... (os error 5)
state [REDACTED_VALUE] backfill is running at [REDACTED_PATH]
Error: failed to initialize sqlite state runtime [REDACTED_VALUE] [REDACTED_PATH]
```

The access-denied fragments came from temporary/PATH setup warnings. They do not establish the cause of the later fatal SQLite initialization error. The exact underlying SQLite cause and error code remain unknown. This report does not claim database corruption, a lock conflict, a stale backfill lease, or a confirmed backfill timeout.

A supported per-launch `sqlite_home` pointing to an owned workspace state directory was previously tested. It did not produce successful initialization. It was not promoted into a model runner.

Observed workflow, rather than a separately validated portable minimal reproducer:

1. Launch the installed native `codex-cli 0.160.1` executable with the `app-server` subcommand, binary stdio pipes, the original working directory, and the existing restrictive tool/network/sandbox overrides.
2. For the previously tested candidate, keep the original arguments and add only the supported per-launch `sqlite_home` location in an owned workspace directory. Do not redirect authentication or replace existing native state.
3. Send exactly one schema-valid `initialize` request containing the required client metadata. Do not send account, thread, or turn methods.
4. Read stdout/stderr with bounded capture and a 45-second watchdog.
5. In the retained probe, observe stdout EOF and native exit 1 at 30.313 seconds without an initialization reply, accompanied by the sanitized backfill/SQLite symptoms above.

The app-server should complete its initialization handshake under a supported execution policy, or return actionable startup diagnostics that preserve the underlying failure while protecting private values. A supported state-directory option should not be treated as a successful workaround until an initialization reply is verified.

**Local observer repair:** the initial sanitizer overredacted the fatal wrapper `failed to initialize sqlite state runtime under <path>: <cause>`. Its unquoted Windows path pattern consumed the same-line cause as well as the path. This was a defect in our local observation code, not an asserted upstream Codex logging defect. Twelve focused offline tests passed with zero failures or errors; native process and socket dispatch were blocked. Those synthetic tests verify the observer, not the native startup bug. The discarded historical cause cannot be recovered from the old sanitized receipt.

```text
windows unelevated restricted-token sandbox cannot enforce split writable root sets directly; refusing to run unsandboxed
```

items.body:
## Summary

Cloud working files and browser state have repeatedly disappeared during ongoing ChatGPT dot tasks. This report consolidates **four documented observation episodes across two dot work contexts, from October 6–8, 2026 (UTC)**.

The strongest recent observation is a previously populated cloud workspace becoming almost empty while the same working-directory path still existed. Multiple workers then found their files missing. Browser state also changed: a previously used tab was absent and the expected Firefox installation was unavailable.

This is a report of observed content loss and discontinuity. The evidence does **not** establish whether the cause is environment replacement, mount loss, rollback, cleanup, migration, or another infrastructure failure. Four observation episodes do not prove four independent backend resets.

## Environment and evidence scope

- ChatGPT dots using a Linux cloud execution environment, shell/file tools, parallel workers, and a cloud browser/desktop.
- Both task-local scratch and shared working areas were affected in the latest episode.
- Firefox 157.0.1 was reported reinstalled after earlier browser loss. Chromium remained available.
- Native work on a separately connected Mac survived the latest cloud incident.
- Exact backend deployment, container/VM identity, storage configuration, and client builds at each incident are unavailable.
- Earlier episodes in the second context were checked against its actual user-visible conversation. Those are dated assistant observation/recovery reports, not independently recovered low-level execution logs.
- Dates below use UTC timestamps from the retained record or the conversation DOM's datetime attributes. Browser-local date labels were not treated as UTC.

## Documented episodes

### 1. October 6, 2026, 01:45:55 UTC: cloud working directory and document draft unavailable

In the second dot context, the assistant reported that the cloud working directory had become unavailable, including the current local DOCX draft.

A subsequent report said all **11 previously saved Library archives survived**, with **389,042,262 bytes rechecked**, but the latest DOCX could not be found among accessible files or in Library because it had existed only in the working directory.

At **03:11:42 UTC**, the assistant reported saving and downloading a reconstructed draft and its rebuild inputs from Library. It explicitly described recovery as incomplete: some earlier source links and source samples were still missing.

**Evidence limit:** The messages establish reported loss of access, unsuccessful draft recovery, and reconstruction. They do not prove permanent physical deletion or identify the infrastructure cause.

### 2. October 7, 2026, between 04:10:24 and 04:35:19 UTC: Firefox installation and profile disappear

In the same second context, the assistant reported that the Firefox installation it had just been using was no longer present; only a fresh Chromium window was available.

It then reported that the exact previous Firefox profile location was also gone and described the current desktop as a different runtime with no Firefox profile. A later message reported reinstalling Firefox 157.0.1. The prior browser extension/configuration had not been restored.

**Timestamp limit:** These loss messages are grouped without their own exposed datetime; the interval above is bounded by adjacent timestamped messages. It is not an exact reset time.

**Evidence limit:** This is verified conversation evidence. Runtime replacement was the assistant's interpretation; no backend lifecycle event or original profile-store audit is available.

### 3. October 7, 2026, 05:57:47 UTC: working files missing while original cwd remains

In the first context, a retained event record documents preexisting cloud working files being absent while the original current-working-directory path remained present. Source code and execution/verification receipts became unavailable. The user was notified at **05:58:04 UTC**.

A later record documents an official Firefox 157.0.1 reinstall at **06:23:34 UTC** after the prior cloud/browser installation disappeared.

The browser recovery is also described in the existing public issue [#51608](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/51608). That issue concerns approval handling during certificate restoration; this report concerns the underlying workspace/browser content-loss symptom. No common root cause with its approval behavior is established.

**Evidence limit:** These are retained incident/recovery records. The cause and whether every missing byte was permanently lost are unknown.

### 4. October 8, 2026, 17:35:32 UTC onward: widespread loss during active parallel work

At **17:35:32 UTC**, a worker reported task directories disappearing following an execution-transport disconnect.

At **17:38:51 UTC**, a logging write failed with `ENOENT` because its previously existing output location was missing.

Read-only checks found:
- The original cwd still existed.
- Scratch and shared working areas contained mount placeholders rather than their previous task contents.
- Multiple workers independently found their source/report directories missing and reported no intentional deletion or rename.
- A previously used browser tab was absent while an older existing tab remained; the expected Firefox installation was unavailable.

Affected classes included source files, implementation drafts, test/qualification inputs, verification reports, and uncheckpointed work. This stopped dependent reviews and required artifact recovery.

A previously saved Library checkpoint was retrieved and verified byte-for-byte. Newer log entries could be reconstructed from prior observations, but their lost original evidence bytes were explicitly **not** claimed recovered. Source recovery remained partial as of this report. Work saved on the separate Mac survived.

**Evidence limit:** The transport disconnect preceded the observation; causation is unproved. Reports of no intentional deletion are worker observations, not a complete infrastructure audit. Browser-state discontinuity alone does not prove snapshot rollback.

## Related observations that are not counted as additional data-loss episodes

- October 6: an execution process-creation failure reported an execution-server transport disconnect and an unknown session. A later read-only command succeeded in the expected workspace. That record did not establish filesystem loss.
- October 7, within a 06:11:55–07:23:00 UTC conversation interval: the second context reported several research workers losing their cloud connection simultaneously. It did not independently establish another file-loss event.
- A later worker-continuity interruption on October 8 left recovered filesystem contents present. It is not counted as new data loss.

## Impact

- Uncheckpointed source and document work must be recreated.
- Previously verified local evidence becomes unavailable, so prior checks cannot simply be reasserted.
- Browser installation/profile loss interrupts workflows and requires reinstalling and reconfiguring tools.
- Long-running multi-worker work is diverted into repeated recovery.
- Library copies proved useful for saved artifacts, but they did not contain every in-progress draft or the latest local evidence.

## Expected behavior

Working files should remain available for the active task under the documented persistence contract. If an environment must be replaced or a storage mount cannot be restored, the task should receive an explicit lifecycle/error event, a clear recovery route, and protection against silently continuing with an apparently valid but empty workspace.

Browser installations and profiles should either survive according to the supported contract or their reset should be clearly disclosed. The product should make the durable location for in-progress work unambiguous.

## Reproduction and investigation request

There is no deterministic minimal reproducer yet. The observed sequence is:

1. Work normally in a dot cloud environment, creating source files, reports, and drafts; use a browser during the same ongoing task.
2. Continue long-running work, including parallel workers.
3. Encounter an execution connection interruption or later resume normal access.
4. Find that previously existing files/directories or browser installation/profile state are missing, despite continuing in the same task and sometimes the same cwd.

Please correlate the UTC windows above with environment lifecycle, reconnect, storage-mount, snapshot/restore, and cleanup events. In particular, investigate why an existing cwd can remain while its task data and shared-area contents are gone, and whether the browser and filesystem discontinuities share an underlying event.

Please also document the actual persistence/recovery guarantees and surface a precise diagnostic when continuity cannot be preserved.

## Follow-up verification (October 8, approximately 18:36 UTC)

The exec workspace and the visible cloud desktop were verified to be separate environments: a harmless temporary marker created through exec was not present in the desktop terminal. Exec-side installation checks alone therefore cannot establish the desktop's browser state.

A separate read-only check in the actual desktop terminal found no Firefox command on PATH and no installation at the previously relevant standard or user-local binary locations. A legacy profile-path check was also empty. Further inspection established that the currently active Firefox profile uses an XDG configuration location instead. No pre-restoration census of that XDG location exists, so whether it previously existed or was lost is UNKNOWN. The latest incident therefore establishes working-file loss and an unavailable expected Firefox installation, but does not independently establish loss of the actual XDG profile. These checks are not an exhaustive all-disk absence claim. No browser reinstall or cross-environment check is counted as another data-loss episode.

## Privacy

This report intentionally contains only sanitized technical observations, timestamps, generic affected artifact classes, and recovery limits. It includes no private project titles or contents, filesystem paths, account/conversation/task IDs or URLs, credentials, network addresses, signed download links, private rules, source code, or raw logs.

## 不具合の概要

同梱のDataプラグインで、Source InspectorのReporting periodとデータプレビューが、オフセット付きの時刻を常にUTCの日付へ変換します。`+09:00` では日付が前日になり、プレビューでは時分秒とオフセットも落ちます。表示にUTCの説明がないため、日本時間の履歴を監査する際、元データと異なる日付が根拠の表示に現れました。

Codex本体の推論バグではなく、同梱プラグインの表示実装の報告です。別の担当リポジトリが適切なら、振り分け先を案内してください。

## 環境

- macOS 26.3 / Apple Silicon、実行環境のタイムゾーン `Asia/Tokyo`
- Codex 26.1002.52244、build 13536（2026-10-09にインストール情報を読取）
- 同梱プラグイン：`data-analytics/1.0.11`
- 対象：Data app base template

## 最小再現

生成したData appの `src` を基準に、同梱コードの関数を直接呼ぶ合成試験です。実データは不要です。

```js
import { reviewedDateRange } from './src/source-provenance.js';
import { displayValue } from './src/charting/chart-theme.js';

const timestamp = '2026-10-09T02:05:36+09:00';
console.log(Intl.DateTimeFormat().resolvedOptions().timeZone);
console.log(reviewedDateRange(
  [{ event_time_jst: timestamp }],
  { query: { reportingField: 'event_time_jst' } },
));
console.log(displayValue(timestamp));
console.log(displayValue('2026-10-09'));
```

同梱の未変更コードに対して実行した結果：

```text
Asia/Tokyo
Oct 8, 2026
Oct 8, 2026
Oct 9, 2026
```

Reporting periodとデータプレビューで前日表示になることは、生成レポートのブラウザ表示でも確認しました。文字列の表記言語はロケール次第ですが、日付が8日になることが問題です。

## 実装上の確認

- `src/source-provenance.js` の `reviewedDateRange` は `Intl.DateTimeFormat` の `timeZone` を `"UTC"` に固定している。
- `src/charting/chart-theme.js` の `displayValue` は日付形式に見える文字列全般をUTCの年月日にし、ISO datetimeでも時刻とオフセットを落とす。
- `src/components/SourceInspector.jsx` はこれらを利用している。

## 期待する動作

- date-onlyと、時刻・オフセットを持つdatetimeを区別する。
- Reporting periodは宣言した業務タイムゾーンで計算・表示できる。UTCを採用する場合もUTCであることを明記する。
- データプレビューでは、datetimeの時刻とタイムゾーンを保持するか、原値を容易に確認できる。
- `2026-10-09T02:05:36+09:00` を日本時間の9日の事象として扱うレポートで、根拠画面が無説明で8日と表示しない。

## 一時回避

生成成果物側で業務日付の列を別途持ち、`query.reportingField` にそのdate-only列を指定しました。また、時刻列を日付自動変換の対象にならない明示的な日本時間の文字列にしました。これは成果物単位の回避で、同梱コードが修正されたことを意味しません。

## 改善要望

Dotsを窓口に複数のCodexチャット、継続Goal、定期実行を動かす場合、その窓口が開始・管理した範囲を一括停止し、対象ごとの実停止を確認できる操作が必要です。

公式の[Dotsの操作説明](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/dots/controls)では、Pauseが現在の主タスクを止める操作であり、委任済み作業や将来の定期実行をすべて止めるものではないと説明されています。その仕様に反する不具合だとは主張しません。利用者の「この窓口に頼んだ仕事を全部止める」を、複数の個別停止操作と自然言語の返答に頼らず実現する改善要求です。

## 実際に起きた状況（匿名化）

2026-10-09、日本時間の会話記録：

| 時刻 | 記録された状態 |
|---|---|
| 02:05:36 | 利用者が関連する全作業の停止を要求 |
| 02:07:22 | 統括が一部の停止指示がキャンセルされ、全停止未確認と報告 |
| 02:13:21 | 統括が直接強制停止する操作を使えず、全停止未完了と報告 |
| 02:16:31 | 9担当への停止指示の受理、うち2担当の停止返答を報告。他担当と正式Goalは未確認 |
| 02:20:49 | 利用者が自分で停止したと申告 |
| 02:20:58 | 統括が自分で停止できたような説明を訂正 |

最初の要求から利用者の介入申告までは15分13秒です。これは実停止の所要時間ではなく、すべての作業がその間継続していた証明でもありません。問題は、利用者が停止状態を確認できず、自分で複数の実行を管理し直す必要があったことです。

## 求める操作

1. この窓口が開始・管理する関連タスク、明示的に管理対象へ加えたチャット、Goal、定期実行の範囲を表示する。
2. その範囲で新たな起動・再起動を抑止してから、実行中ターンを停止する。
3. 対象Goalをpauseし、対象定期実行をdisableする。無関係な利用者の作業は操作しない。
4. 対象ごとに `request accepted`、`turn stopped/idle`、`goal paused`、`schedule disabled`、`unreachable`、`failed` を独立して読戻す。
5. 一部しか止められていない場合は完了扱いせず、未確認の対象と利用者が行える操作を表示する。

1つの窓口から、通常チャット2件、継続Goal1件、定期実行1件を開始する。うち1つを一時的に到達不能にし、範囲指定の停止を行う。停止済み対象と未確認対象が分かれ、停止後に対象の定期実行が新規ターンを開始せず、範囲外のチャットは継続することを確認する。

これは「steerの受理は必ず実行停止を意味する」という仕様違反の主張ではありません。自然言語の停止指示だけに依存する担当移管では、実行競合を防げないという設計上の問題です。

## 実際に起きた状況（匿名化）

2026-10-08、日本時間：

- 13:14、13:18ごろ：旧担当Aへの保留・停止指示が `steered` として受理された。
- 統括はこの受理を前提に、新担当Bへ同じ送信業務の移管を進めた。
- 13:26ごろ：旧担当Aから送信完了の報告が届いた。
- 統括は新担当Bへ、追加送信を止めて確認だけにするよう急いで指示した。

担当側の受信記録と完了報告を照合しました。二重送信が実際に発生したことは確認していません。確実に確認できるのは、旧担当の停止完了が確定する前に新担当を有効にした競合です。外部サービスの現在状態をこの調査で再検証したわけでもありません。

## 望ましい契約

- 指示の `accepted / queued` と、適用済み `applied`、実行終了 `idle`、置換済み `superseded`、失敗を区別する。
- 旧担当への `cancel-and-await` のような操作で、停止要求と実停止確認を結ぶ。
- 同じ論理操作に操作IDと所有世代を結び、移管後は旧世代からの新規コミットを拒否する。外部サービスが対応する場合は冪等キーとも連携する。
- すでに外部操作がコミット済みなら、その実績を照合して新担当へ渡す。取消で過去の外部操作が巻き戻るとは扱わない。
- 成否不明なら、新担当に再実行させる前に照合が必要な状態として返す。
- 操作先がブラウザや任意コネクターで共通の実行制御が難しい場合も、保証できる範囲と、協調停止に過ぎない範囲を明示する。

## 合成の回帰試験案（未実行）

実メールを使わず、モックのカウンターへのコミットで試せます。

1. Aが操作ID Xを担当し、コミット直前の待機点に入る。
2. 統括がAへ停止を要求する。
3. 停止要求の受理だけをもとにBへXを移す状況を作る。
4. AとBを解放する。
5. 新担当の有効化が旧担当の停止・実績確認まで待機すること、移管済みの旧世代では新規コミットできないことを検証する。
6. 停止前にAがすでにコミットした場合は、Bによる追加コミットを避ける。

## 環境・関連

Dotsから複数Codexチャットへ指示を渡す構成で発生しました。10月8日の事象当時のアプリ版は未確認です。報告時に同じMacで読めたインストール情報はmacOS 26.3 / Apple Silicon、Codex 26.1002.52244、build 13536であり、これを過去の実行版と断定しません。

関連：#30499 の非割込みキューと配送状態、#38289 のidle条件付きturn開始。今回求めるのは配送方法だけでなく、旧担当と新担当の間の外部操作権の移管と重複防止です。

公開本文は匿名化した時系列と合成試験案のみで、宛先・本文・私有チャットID・生ログは含めません。

items.body:
## Summary

In the unified ChatGPT/Codex **macOS desktop app**, ordinary **Chat mode** intermittently fails to render the **entire final assistant response** in the currently open conversation window. The sidebar preview may already contain the beginning of the generated final answer, but selecting that conversation shows only the `Worked for …` activity/thinking section. The final-answer region **below** that section is completely absent.

Opening **File → New Window** and navigating to the same conversation immediately restores the normal view: `Worked for …` followed by the complete final answer. No application restart is needed.

**Important distinction:** This is **not** the final response being rendered *inside* the `Worked for` section. Expanding that section shows the expected interim commentary, tools/search activity, and status. The separate final response itself is missing from the affected window.

## Environment

- App: Unified ChatGPT/Codex desktop app on macOS, **regular Chat mode** (not a local Codex task or Quick Chat floating window).
- Desktop client version: **26.1002.52244**, reported by the session's desktop client identifier; exact About-dialog build number not independently checked.
- Platform: macOS, Apple Silicon (exact OS version not collected).
- Subscription: ChatGPT Pro.
- Observed: October 8, 2026.
- Frequency: Intermittent, recurring across conversations; not claimed to be deterministic.

## Steps / observed sequence

1. Open or continue an ordinary Chat-mode conversation in the macOS desktop app.
2. Send a prompt and wait while the assistant generates a response.
3. The conversation's sidebar preview can show the beginning of the generated answer.
4. Select/open that conversation in the current window. The view displays `Worked for …` and its proper activity, but **no final response below it**.
5. Expanding/collapsing `Worked for …` does not reveal the final answer: it contains distinct interim content, not the final answer.
6. Without quitting the app, choose **File → New Window** and reopen the same conversation there.
7. The full final answer now appears **beneath** `Worked for …`, as expected.

The reporter confirmed step 6–7 resolves the problem. Restarting the application has also recovered the content but is impractical when concurrent long-running Codex tasks are active.

## Expected vs. actual

**Expected:** Once a response is completed, the current Chat view renders its final assistant message below the completed `Worked for` section, consistent with the sidebar preview and persisted conversation. Switching back to a conversation should not hide the finished answer.

**Actual:** The final answer is completely missing from the active window's message display, even though the sidebar preview has shown it. The separate working/activity section renders correctly. A freshly opened window loads and displays the missing answer.

This suggests a window-local rendering/conversation-state synchronization problem, but **no root cause has been verified**. No claim that the response was deleted or that its contents were reclassified into the activity section.

## Impact and workaround

This interrupts routine Chat use and makes successfully completed responses look empty. Repeated full restarts are especially costly/risky for a user running long-lived Codex tasks at the same time.

**Non-destructive workaround confirmed:** `File → New Window`, then open the affected conversation in that new window. It restores the response without closing/restarting the app.

The reporter has screenshots of the *recovered* state in both collapsed and expanded `Worked for` views showing the final answer properly below the activity. A screenshot of the *missing-answer state* was not captured for this report; no private conversation screenshot is attached publicly.

## Related reports (similar symptoms, distinct surfaces/recovery)

- **#49062 (Windows desktop):** Completed responses are invisible until conversation reopen; that report also describes hangs and a `Couldn't load messages` error. The macOS incident here has no such observed loading error and is reliably restored by **a new app window**.
- **#51919 (macOS Quick Chat):** On the same 26.1002.52244 desktop version, the floating Quick Chat surface shows activity without a completed answer. This report concerns **ordinary Chat in the main application window**, with a confirmed New Window recovery.
- **#41948 (previously closed):** Describes final content being grouped *inside* `Worked for`. Here the working section contains *different, appropriate progress content*, and the separate final answer is wholly absent from the broken window.

Please evaluate whether these share a desktop message-projection/window-state cause while keeping the distinct UI behavior and recovery paths visible.

Codex desktop cannot connect to my Windows SSH host, although ordinary SSH authentication and PowerShell commands work. The problem also reproduces under a newly created Windows user profile.

- Neither action resolved the issue.

1. Close Codex.

3. Verify that zero matching directories remain in LocalCache.

Codex for Windows should launch successfully and remain stable when signing in with either ChatGPT Pro account.

items.body:
## What variant of Codex are you using?

Codex CLI/TUI. The same interaction would also be useful in the IDE extension and desktop app wherever image-viewing tool activity is displayed.

## What feature would you like to see?

Make the image path in image-viewing tool activity a clickable link that opens the image in a browser or local image viewer.

For example, when Codex inspects a local image, the activity/history entry may look like:

```text
Viewed image (/some/image.png)
```

The image path (or the entire “Viewed image” label) should be clickable. Clicking it should open that exact image using an available image preview, browser, or the operating system's default image viewer. The important part is being able to inspect the same image Codex just looked at without copying the path and opening it manually.

### Why this is useful

When working with screenshots, CAD drawings, detection overlays, or generated reports, Codex may inspect several images during a task. These activity entries are a natural place for the user to open the corresponding files and verify the analysis. Asking Codex to repeat every image path as a link in its final answer should not be necessary.

### Expected behavior

- Image-viewing tool entries expose an openable image link directly in the activity/history UI, not only in final assistant responses.
- Opening happens only after an explicit user click; viewing an image with a tool should not automatically launch another application.
- In the CLI, use terminal-native hyperlinks (such as OSC 8) where supported, with a readable/copyable path fallback. Terminal/file-URI handling varies, so provide an explicit open action where needed rather than assuming every terminal opens local image links correctly.
- In the IDE/app, use an appropriate image preview or local-file opener rather than treating the image as a source-code file.
- Resolve relative paths against the tool call's working directory; preserve the full target when the displayed path is shortened.
- Handle spaces, Unicode and special characters correctly.
- If the file is missing or is on a remote host that cannot be opened locally, report that clearly rather than opening an unrelated local path.
- Keep links usable when revisiting activity history or resuming a session, as long as the underlying file remains accessible.

## Additional information

This request is specifically about **image-viewing tool activity entries**, including images Codex inspects internally while working. It does not require inline image rendering or a thumbnail.

Related requests found during duplicate checking:

- #35824 requests inline previews for images referenced in final responses and explicitly excludes images opened internally. This request instead makes those internal image-viewing activity entries actionable.
- #31554 concerns OSC 8 rendering for ordinary Markdown links. That support could help implement the CLI part, but the requested link here should be created by the tool-activity renderer itself.

The example path above is illustrative and contains no private project data.

| Local timezone | America/Sao_Paulo (UTC-03:00) |

Hardware and OS values were read locally using `system_profiler` and `sw_vers`. Serial numbers, hardware UUIDs, account identifiers, private conversation IDs, credentials, and user paths are omitted.

### What issue are you seeing?

Codex has been making my entire computer noticeably sluggish, sometimes to the point of freezing when I start an ordinary task. I have used Codex since its first version on the same computer, with the same usual applications open.

**The slowdown did not begin on October 8. It had already been happening for some time; October 8 was when I finally investigated it, with AI assistance. The exact onset and first affected app version are unknown.**

I had created a recurring scheduled task / heartbeat well before this investigation. From my perspective, it was no longer executing as expected, and I had forgotten about that. It was nevertheless still marked `ACTIVE`. This was an existing task, not a new task created on the day the problem was diagnosed. Its execution history was not independently audited.

The investigation found a high-frequency `maybe_resume_skipped_inactive_hotkey_window` loop in a hidden, unfocused renderer. The `conversationId` repeated in these events exactly matched the `target_thread_id` of the only active heartbeat.

#### Local log evidence

- **140,964 occurrences** between **2026-10-08T15:57:43.962Z** and **2026-10-08T15:58:17.985Z**: approximately **4.1 thousand events/second** over about 34 seconds.
- Peak observed count: **5,265 events in one second**.
- The events consistently identified renderer web contents ID `3`.
- The native window was hidden and unfocused, while the document visibility field was `visible`.
- The retained log window was only a sample of the problem; it does not establish its total duration.

Sanitized fields from the observed events (an excerpt, not a complete raw log record):

```text
[electron-message-handler] maybe_resume_skipped_inactive_hotkey_window
conversationId=<TARGET_THREAD_ID>
documentVisibilityState=visible
rendererWebContentsId=3
rendererWindowFocused=false
rendererWindowVisible=false
```

The matching heartbeat had:

```text
kind: heartbeat
status before intervention: ACTIVE
target_thread_id: <TARGET_THREAD_ID>
schedule: recurring, twice weekly
status after intervention: PAUSED
```

The same placeholder above represents the exact matching identifier. The event name alone does not establish that this was a hotkey window; I did not independently prove the Page prewarm route in this installation.

#### CPU observations and heartbeat pause

| Observation | Affected renderer CPU | Main app CPU | Resume-loop events |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Initial diagnostic snapshot | 135.9% | 68.3% | Present |
| Immediately before pausing the heartbeat | 127.4% | 58.1% | Present |
| Two follow-up samples after pausing it | Approximately 0.4–0.7% | Approximately 3–7% | 0 observed |

**The app remained open during the heartbeat pause and the immediate verification. These follow-up samples were taken before the later restart.** Pausing the heartbeat preserved the task and schedule rather than deleting it.

This is an observed before/after association in this installation, based on short verification samples rather than a long-duration benchmark. I did not reactivate the task to perform an on/off/on test, so I am not claiming a completely isolated causal proof or a confirmed source-code explanation. CPU percentages are process CPU values as reported on macOS.

#### Separate memory-pressure finding after the CPU loop stopped

Slowness subsequently returned after restarting the Mac/app, even though both automations were still paused and the same loop was absent from the inspected logs. Therefore, pausing the heartbeat did not resolve every source of resource pressure.

- The computer has only 8 GB of RAM. Initial swap observations were approximately **5.7–6.3 GB**.
- A later observation showed approximately **9.4 GB of swap**.
- Numerous Node/MCP helper instances remained associated with inactive sessions. These included Firecrawl, Netlify, computer-use, Node REPL, and app/code-review helpers, with wrapper/child processes.
- **126 helper/subprocesses belonging to inactive sessions were terminated** after identifying their process trees and excluding the current session's helpers. The main app, backend, and current session helpers were preserved. A follow-up check found no surviving processes among those targeted.
- Swap subsequently fell from approximately **9.4 GB to 5.2 GB**, and responsiveness improved according to my direct use of the computer.

The cleanup count is retained in a local action record. The swap values are point-in-time observations, not a controlled benchmark.

This secondary finding should be investigated separately from the renderer loop. It does **not** establish a memory leak, whether session retention was expected, or whether every remaining helper was defective. Ending helpers also releases memory by design. I include it because the severe system-wide slowdown on this 8 GB machine had more than one observed component.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

This is the sequence observed in an existing installation, not a verified reproduction from a clean install:

1. Have an older recurring heartbeat/scheduled task still marked `ACTIVE`, associated with a conversation that is not currently in use.
2. Use or reopen Codex Desktop 26.1002.52244 and start an ordinary task.
3. Inspect process CPU and desktop logs. In this installation, a hidden/unfocused renderer emitted thousands of `maybe_resume_skipped_inactive_hotkey_window` events per second, and its CPU exceeded 100%.
4. Match the event's `conversationId` against the heartbeat's `target_thread_id`.
5. Pause the matching heartbeat through the supported app automation mechanism.
6. Observe whether the event storm stops and the affected renderer returns to low CPU, while the app remains open.

The necessary trigger conditions are still unknown. I have not established whether a missing, deleted, archived, temporary, or remotely stored target conversation is required. I also have not established that every active heartbeat reproduces the problem. The task was left paused to avoid reintroducing the severe slowdown.

### What is the expected behavior?

- An inactive or hidden renderer should settle at low resource usage instead of repeatedly attempting to resume the same conversation thousands of times per second.
- An existing scheduled task that cannot execute normally should surface an actionable state/error and avoid an unbounded retry/log loop.
- Idle session helpers should have a bounded, understandable lifecycle so that ordinary use does not accumulate enough resource usage to make the whole computer unresponsive.
- Pausing a scheduled task should reliably quiesce activity associated with that task.

### Additional information

Related reports, found before submitting this issue:

- #51888 — same inactive-window resume marker and app version; the discussion includes macOS heartbeat observations.
- #52091 — macOS resume-message storm and crashes. **I did not confirm the reported SIGTRAP crash pattern in my own case.**
- #52093 — Windows hidden Pages prewarm renderer analysis. Its proposed source-level explanation was **not independently verified here**.
- [Reddit report posted on October 8, 2026](https://www.reddit.com/r/codex/comments/1x0t5tl/a_forgotten_reminder_was_keeping_codex_at_145_cpu/) — very similar older-reminder / high-CPU pattern. That author's hardware and measurements are separate from mine.

These may represent the same underlying renderer issue. This report adds the local chronology, an older recurring task, matching task/conversation identifiers, before/after measurements without restarting during the pause verification, and the impact on an M1 Mac with 8 GB RAM.

Investigation was AI-assisted. No private task prompts, complete configuration files, authentication material, personal project contents, or unredacted session logs are attached. The original observations above preceded later local MCP startup/configuration experiments; those changes are not presented as part of the heartbeat test. No project dependency cleanup was performed.
